external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone running the mobile app.

external_entities.name: member browser
external_entities.description: A member's browser used to sign in and approve partner app consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company on its own server.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile app used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone. Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that signs members in, handles authorization and issues tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: Nobody decided an idle timeout for the authorization server sign-in.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and processes rewards operations.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: sign in and consent
data_flows.description: A member signs in and approves a partner app's consent screen in the browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen

data_flows.name: token requests
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: client secret and token request data

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The authorization server returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The text describes the browser return path while the authorization code is delivered to the partner app's redirect URI.

data_flows.name: issue access token
data_flows.description: The authorization server provides the mobile app with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores member and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: disconnect partner app
data_flows.description: The mobile app requests disconnection of a partner app through the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app

data_flows.name: delete refresh token
data_flows.description: The authorization server deletes a disconnected partner app's refresh token from the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which deletes that app's refresh token from the identity database

data_flows.name: read and write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write API requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every request it receives, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: obtain access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Nothing happens to that member's refresh tokens, which sit in the same database.
data_flows.data_description: member account closure and refresh token data

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account where the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, outside the organisation's cloud account.

trust_boundaries.name: partner app servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers owned and operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member account information, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds member account data, credentials and authorization records.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store is confidential because it contains requests and headers, which may contain credentials and member-related data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
